item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 15 September 2026
item.description:
Syp is absolutely buzzing over World of Warcraft Forever, calling Blizzard’s Classic Plus reveal a huge, carefully judged evolution of WoW Classic.

Tipa enjoyed RetroWorld Expo, grabbed a retro Polaroid Go 3, and came away charmed by its tiny, muddy instant photos anyway.

Marc makes the case for Chibi-Robo! Plug Into Adventure! as a weird, lovely GameCube gem about cleaning, family dysfunction, and offbeat charm.

Scopique is hooked again by No Man’s Sky COSMOS, even if old save baggage and Sentinel combat still make returning a little messy.

David recaps a brutal Dragonbane megadungeon session as the Battle Brothers push into the Gates of Power and tangle with skeletons and a Death Dog.

Wilhelm reacts to BlizzCon 2026 with surprise and delight that WoW Classic Plus is real as World of Warcraft Forever.

Andrew Plotkin surveys several mystery-shaped games, praising The Mermaid Mask’s dual protagonists while knocking its banter-heavy writing and slow evidence grind.

Heartless breaks down the Packers’ collapse against the Vikings, pinning it more on bad decisions and 29 unanswered points than the refs.

Joel’s weeknotes bounce from Ocarina of Time and a six-hour Play Station podcast to BBQ, coffee, and a handy photo-cleaning app.

Tan uses OpenAI’s claimed Navier-Stokes breakthrough to argue AI-driven math risks stripping the beauty, struggle, and human meaning from mathematics.

Cristian explains why Bitwarden Flatpak wouldn’t talk to Vaultwarden behind Caddy and Tailscale, and how an SSL_CERT_FILE override fixed it.

Brennan tees up a critique of Medium’s shift from human-centered publishing ideals toward a more pro-AI stance.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 14 September 2026
item.description:
Stargrace is mildly tempted by World of Warcraft Forever’s level-60 fresh start after BlizzCon, even if she’s still mostly guild-hunting and gold-making.

Sey introduces Good Game Lobby’s Discord gaming club, where the community nominates short indie picks and is currently playing Firewatch for September.

Bhagpuss riffs on gacha luck across Genshin Impact, Noah’s Heart, Wuthering Waves, and Neverness To Everness, while admitting he rarely wants to swap characters.

Kimimi makes a charming case for Famicom Tetris 2 and BomBliss, loving its homely presentation more than any claim to definitive Tetris greatness.

Owls kicks off Valheim 1.0 with bears, dual-wield Early Axes, a comfy longhouse, and an accidental second Eikthyr kill.

Wes serves a snack-size ROM roundup with fan translation and patch notes, plus links on Witch of the Dark Castle, Saburo Jinguji, Satellaview, and Blue Dragon.

Wilhelm eyes EVE Online’s CSM 21 election with heavy skepticism, arguing CCP keeps sidelining player feedback for force-projection nerfs, HUD changes, and side projects.

Kelly digs into boredom as a lack of fulfilling activity, sketching out different ways people escape it beyond just staying busy.

Warner’s reading roundup circles AI, democracy, geology, and the future of readers themselves, with Bryan Cantrill and Paul Ford among the highlights.

Tobold reflects on fading internet fame, burned-out creators, and why influencer dreams usually don’t translate into lasting financial security.

Roger unloads on bloated, paternalistic software design and nonstop updates, then gives Nintendo’s Switch setup a rare gold star for actually feeling intuitive.

Bruce Schneier says Microsoft’s 972-fix Windows patch shows AI is supercharging vulnerability discovery, and the safe patching window is basically immediate now.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 13 September 2026
item.description:
Frostilyte shares practical Mewgenics starter advice, especially prioritizing Butch upgrades, hoarding gear, and valuing Speed above basically everything.

Krista rounds up late-2026 indie hopes, from Witchbrook and Grave Seasons to Dressmaker, Otterly Lost, and Over The Hill.

Shintar is all-in on Warcraft Classic+, praising BlizzCon’s new zones, raids, race-class combos, visual toggles, and that emotional trailer.

Ellie finds Lil Gator Game tapping straight into 3D platformer nostalgia and the bittersweet pull of recapturing childhood.

Wilhelm returns to Fantasy Critic with score shuffles, as Rhythm Heaven Groove rises and Crimson Moon dings his standing.

The Friendly Necromancer recounts two brutal EverQuest Legends Plane of Hate runs, ending with a maddening rare-creature bug.

Michael finally finishes NES Metroid, praising its weird, mysterious vibe even while grumbling about death recovery and old-school friction.

WCRobinson posts a spoiler-warning Metroid Prime 4: Beyond screenshot gallery, celebrating Samus, bosses, and Viewros’ standout visuals.

Ramen Junkie’s weekly wrap mixes roof work, Transformers finds, McDonald’s Godzilla x Hello Kitty toy hunting, and a couple of books.

Emily recounts a romantic dream featuring Kit Fisto, warm water, a glowing pool, and an underwater kiss into darkness.

Tofutush recaps a packed Xinjiang trip with Kashgar, Tashqurghan, desert rides, altitude, Tajik food, and several excellent animal sightings.

Dave Winer riffs on working with Claude, Frontier scripts, RSS updates, and the messy practical limits of social posting.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 12 September 2026
item.description:
Syp bounces between Fallout 76, Palia, and LOTRO, enjoying newbie generosity, grumbling at character deletion, and dragging his Captain onward.

CrazyKinux says EVE Online is absolutely still worth playing in 2026, if you can love a harsh MMO that wastes your time and fights back.

Bhagpuss rounds up game odds and ends, including a brief, unconvinced look at browser MMO MurderCartel and its slick-but-not-for-me 2D style.

Joel returns to Land of Eem after six months, winging a family TTRPG session with Wally’s Waffles and Rats and a lot less prep than planned.

Anarchae’s weekly digest mixes job-hunt chaos, a Red Cross first-aid course, Yokomizo Seishi, golden-age SF, TV, and some games.

Joar takes stock of post-50 friendship during an Arizona move, finding four real late-night calls rooted in work, college, and swim-parent life.

Jimmy points readers to a new Analog Antiquarian post on the Tudor kings, a quick detour from digital history into worldly wonders.

Cristian shares a photo-journal shot of a flame at a gas pipe for #the100pics, short and purely visual.

Tobold argues Trump’s proposed $5,000 dividend would work best as a tax-the-rich redistribution plan and a sharper Democratic counterplay.

Aneesh bookmarks a video on why your IDE is more than a text editor, calling it a strong setup and a good watch.

Warner sizes up Apple’s latest event, seeing steady iPhone Pro updates and a cautious, maybe-still-niche bet on the folding iPhone Duo.

Wilhelm marks 20 years of blogging by mulling regrets, road-not-taken moments, and his long-running annoyance with the blog’s name.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 11 September 2026
item.description:
Shintar digs through SWTOR Total Galactic War leaderboards to compare server populations, using Conquest points as a practical activity snapshot.

Sey wraps Gamescom with a Battle Vision interview and quick hits on indie standouts like Walk The Frog, Lucky Punk, Rover’s Tale, and Moomin.

Azuriel is 31 hours into Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 and still mostly brewing potions, but the muddy medieval immersion has clearly got its hooks in.

Kimimi revisits Ys VI as Falcom’s big comeback, arguing its 2D-on-3D style and crackling action still feel like a promise fulfilled.

Luna’s August was a blur of Sovereign Tower, ReStory, Big Walk, and more, with cozy management sims and co-op puzzling carrying the month.

Oya rounds up a packed summer of Ghost Trick, Big Walk, reviews, and books, with the clear takeaway that Ghost Trick absolutely won people over.

Zack says MIO: Memories in Orbit looks gorgeous and has intriguing sci-fi lore, but its punishing difficulty makes this Metroidvania a frustrating climb.

Wilhelm kicks off TAGN’s 20th anniversary by trimming two decades of game coverage into a top-20 list and explaining how categories differ from tags.

Axxuy reflects on parks, trails, and forests to argue that even “nature” is often a carefully built environment, not untouched wilderness.

Brennan reflects on 9/11’s long cultural shadow, from fear and war to internet-era media, memory, conspiracy, and how later generations inherit it.

Roger tackles a film questionnaire with favorites, grudges, quotes, and scenes, mixing classic cinema appreciation with some gloriously scrappy personal picks.

Kelly swaps aging ReadyNAS and Time Capsule gear for a Synology 925+, praising DSM and SMB-friendly backups while noting one looming caveat.
